body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0; background: #f6f7f9; color: #1d1f23; } .top { background: #1d4ed8; color: white; padding: 1rem 2rem; } main { max-width: 640px; margin: 2rem auto; display: grid; gap: 1.5rem; } .card { background: white; border-radius: 8px; padding: 1.25rem; box-shadow: 0 1px 3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); } form label { display: block; margin-top: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; } form input { width: 100%; padding: 0.5rem; box-sizing: border-box; } input:invalid { border: 2px solid #dc2626; background: #fef2f2; } .help-icon { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 1.2em; height: 1.2em; border-radius: 50%; background: #e5e7eb; font-size: 0.8em; cursor: help; } #task-list { list-style: none; margin: 0; } #task-list li { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; padding: 0.5rem 0; border-bottom: 1px solid #eee; } button { cursor: pointer; } const list = document.getElementById('task-list'); const form = document.getElementById('add-form'); list.addEventListener('click', (event) => { const button = event.target.closest('button.delete'); if (!button) return; button.closest('li').remove(); }); form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => { event.preventDefault(); if (!form.checkValidity()) return; const title = form.elements.title.value.trim(); const li = document.createElement('li'); const id = String(Date.now()); li.dataset.id = id; li.innerHTML = ` `; li.querySelector('span').textContent = title; list.append(li); form.reset(); });

content.text:
I added the dark theme by editing the three existing files. I didn't open it in a browser or run any checks on it; a request to syntax-check `app.js` was declined.

**What it does**
- **Default:** the page follows the operating system's light/dark setting and switches live if that setting changes.
- **Header button:** labelled "Theme: System / Light / Dark". Each click moves to the next option in that order, and screen readers are told which option comes next.
- **Remembers the choice:** Light and Dark are saved in the browser. Choosing System deletes the saved value, so the page follows the OS again. If the browser blocks storage, such as in some private modes, the toggle still works for that visit.
- **No flash on load:** a small script in the `<head>` of `index.html` applies the saved theme before the page appears, so it doesn't load in the wrong theme first.

**Changes by file**
- **`style.css`:** the hard-coded colours are now named colour variables, with a light and a dark value for each. The page follows the OS by default, and the button can force light or dark. The browser also uses this to switch the built-in controls (inputs and the date picker) to match. The red invalid-field highlight, the help icon and the list dividers each have a dark version. The header now lays out the title and button side by side.
- **`index.html`:** adds the toggle button to the header and the early-load script.
- **`app.js`:** adds the toggle logic at the top. The task code is unchanged.

**Browser support:** the CSS uses `light-dark()`, which works in current Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari (since 2024). Older browsers won't show the colours correctly.

**Light-mode change:** the only visual change in light mode is the header layout.
